title: Bills filed to raise Texas minimum wage to $15 an hour
excerpt: Two bills filed ahead of the 2027 Texas legislative session would raise the state's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour, a change that would take effect September 1, 2027 if approved. Texas has held at $7.25 since 2009.
content:
Two bills filed ahead of the 2027 Texas legislative session would raise the state's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour, a change that would take effect September 1, 2027 if approved.

State Rep. Armando Walle, a Democrat from Houston, filed House Bill 132, and State Rep. Ana-María Rodríguez Ramos filed House Bill 110. Both would require employers to pay workers at least $15 an hour, or the federal minimum wage if it is higher.

Texas has no minimum wage of its own, so the federal rate of $7.25 an hour applies — a rate that has not changed since 2009.

A third proposal, House Bill 246, would raise the rate to $17 an hour.

The bills were among the first filed when bill prefiling opened Monday, November 9, for the 90th Texas Legislature, which convenes January 12, 2027. Lawmakers have until March 12 to file most bills, and any wage bill would still need to pass both chambers and be signed by the governor before it could take effect.

Sources: Hammrod News Laredo TX, November 9, 2026; bill filing coverage, November 10, 2026.
